newsitem.title: USA: Aetna sees '97 cost ratio in line with '96.
newsitem.headline: Aetna sees '97 cost ratio in line with '96.

text.p: Aetna U.S. Healthcare Chief Financial Officer James Dickerson expects medical cost loss ratio for 1997 to be lower than the fourth quarter 1996 ratio of 83.1 percent and more in line with the full year's ratio of 79.9 percent.
Speaking to analysts at a Smith Barney Health Care Services conference, he said "we don't expect the 83.1 (percent) to continue."

During the presentation he said the company expected premiums to go up by three to 10 percent depending on the product and the geographical area. He said premiums are expected to be in excess of the medical costs.

In answer to an analyst's question, he said, he was not greatly concerned with Medicare and Medicaid reform possibilities saying it had not dampened the company's views on the opportunity for top-line and earnings growth from Medicare.
"It's a long way from a politician saying something to media and law becoming law," he said.
He added that Medicare was not a product the company had to offer and was therefore not something it was locked into.
Dickerson said there were currently 37 million people eligible for Medicare and it was projected that about 50 percent of these would move to HMOs by 2000.
He said the company saw opportunity in this area and was currently in 14 states covering about 45 percent of Medicare eligibles. He added that Aetna planned to file in three more states this year.
Aetna U.S. Healthcare is the healthcare division of insurance company Aetna Inc.
